Tutorials/WepManTypes: Use the on-screen controls. Try the knife and pistol first.
Tutorials/WepManImIntro: Select a weapon with its on-screen icon, then use <RED>aim, fire and reload</>. The backpack icon opens the inventory.
Tutorials/WepManImKnifeInfo: Tap the <Red>knife</> icon, then fire: one press performs a full slash; holding repeats slashes.
Tutorials/WepManImPistolInfo: Tap the <Red>weapon</> icon to equip your pistol. Hold aim and tap fire to shoot.
Tutorials/WepManImWatchInfo: Hold the round health dial to raise your left hand and check health and ammunition on your wrist. Release to lower your hand.
Tutorials/HelpInfoInventory:
Hold an item with your finger and drag it to an empty space. Release your finger to place it.

To use a healing item, drag it to the green heart that appears on the right and release. Back closes the inventory.
UIStrings/CustomizeHandedness: <Default.Text>Choose the character's dominant hand. This setting determines where weapons and equipment are placed.</>
UIStrings/CustomizeSitStandDesc: <Default.Text>Choose the character's initial camera height profile.</>
UIStrings/CustomizeComfortModeDesc: <Default.Text>Use the floating movement stick and swipe the right side of the screen to look around.</>
DeathStrings/MainAshleyHealQuick: Healing items restore Ashley's health. Keep an eye on her condition.
DeathStrings/MainAshleyDumpster: Ashley is safe from danger while she hides in a dumpster.
DeathStrings/MainAshleyCommand: Ashley can wait or follow you: tap the Ashley icon at the top of the screen. Keep her away from enemies.
DeathStrings/MainHealingItems: Healing items restore health. Check your supplies in the inventory.
DeathStrings/MercHealSlots: Healing items restore health. Check your supplies in the inventory.
DeathStrings/MainQuickTeleportBack: To move away from enemies, pull the <Red>floating stick</> on the left side of the screen down.
DeathStrings/MercTeleport: To move away from enemies, pull the <Red>floating stick</> on the left side of the screen down.
DeathStrings/MainQuick180Turn: Swipe quickly on the <Red>right half of the screen</> to turn further. Slow swipes keep precise aiming.
DeathStrings/MercQuickTurn: Swipe quickly on the <Red>right half of the screen</> to turn further. Slow swipes keep precise aiming.
Options/CutsceneQTEsDesc:
Cutscene QTEs
QTEs require a quick response to the on-screen prompt.

Disable them to watch cutscenes without additional actions.
PlayingManual/QTEInfo:
QTEs require a quick response to the on-screen prompts.

Cutscene QTEs can be disabled in General Settings.
UIStrings/CustomizePopupComfortDesc: Move with the floating stick and look around by swiping the right side of the screen.
PlayingManual/HealingInfo: Protect Ashley: if she is taken away or killed, the game ends. Healing items can restore her health. Your shots can also hurt her, so aim carefully.
PlayingManual/HealingConsumablesImageTex: Select healing items with the medical bag icon at the top of the screen.
PlayingManual/ReloadingImageText1: Reload includes magazine ejection and chambering.
PlayingManual/ReloadingInfo: Tap the <Red>reload</> icon with a gun equipped. The weapon ejects its magazine, receives ammunition and completes its normal loading animation. Wait for the reload to finish before firing. Different weapons use their own magazines or shells.
PlayingManual/ChamberingInfo: Weapons keep their own loading mechanisms. Shotguns complete the pump action after firing; rifles use their normal bolt action. After reloading, chambering is completed before the next shot. You do not need a separate chambering control.
PlayingManual/GrenadesInfo: Assign a grenade to its inventory slot, then tap the <Red>grenade</> icon. Aim by swiping the right side of the screen, then tap fire to throw. The pin and throwing motion are handled by the weapon's normal animation.
PlayingManual/KnifeInfo: Tap the <Red>knife</> icon, then fire. One press performs one full slash; holding repeats slashes. Wait for a slash to finish before pressing again. The knife can break containers and conserve ammunition, but close combat leaves you vulnerable.
PlayingManual/ImmersiveInfo: Select equipped weapons and items with their on-screen icons. The selected item stays in the character's hand. Assign equipment in the inventory before selecting it during gameplay.
PlayingManual/QuickSelectInfo: Tap the on-screen icon for the assigned handgun, long gun, grenade or healing item. The knife has its own icon. Empty equipment slots cannot be selected. You do not need to hold a separate button to keep an item equipped.
PlayingManual/MoveAndTurnInfo: Move with the <Red>floating stick</> on the left. Swipe the <Red>right side of the screen</> to look around. Movement follows the direction of the camera. Turning is continuous.
PlayingManual/MoveAndTurnFlavorText: Adjust your pace with the floating stick.
PlayingManual/TeleportInfo: The mobile controls use continuous movement. Drag the floating stick on the left to walk, strafe or move backwards. Swipe the right side to turn.
PlayingManual/TeleportMovieText: Use the floating stick to move.
PlayingManual/ContextActionsInfo: When an action such as a kick, jump or helping Ashley becomes available, its on-screen prompt appears. Tap <Red>action</> to perform the available action.
PlayingManual/InteractionsInfo: Approach an object with an interaction indicator and use <Red>action</>. Follow the current on-screen prompt. Some interactions require you to remain close to the object until the action is finished.
PlayingManual/CommandingInfo: Ashley follows you through the adventure. She can follow or wait, and some locations offer context actions such as hiding. Keep her away from enemies and watch her condition.
PlayingManual/UseKeyItemInfo: Some barriers require a key or puzzle piece. Use <Red>action</> at the lock, then select the appropriate item in the displayed panel and place it where required.
PlayingManual/CombineInfo: Hold an inventory item with your finger, drag it onto a compatible item and release to combine them. Combining can save space, create new items or attach weapon parts. Use the link icon for attached parts.
PlayingManual/AssignInfo: Drag a weapon, grenade or healing item onto its matching equipment slot. The four slots hold a handgun, a long gun, a grenade and a healing item. Ammunition is associated with weapons automatically.
PlayingManual/AssignImageFlavorText: Drag an item onto its matching equipment slot.
PlayingManual/HealingConsumablesInfo: Tap the <Red>medical bag</> icon at the top of the screen, then hold fire to use the item in your hand. You can also heal in the inventory by dragging a healing item onto the character's health portrait and releasing it.
PlayingManual/HealInInventoryInfo: The inventory lets you heal while the game is paused. Hold a healing item with your finger, drag it onto the character's health portrait on the right and release it.
PlayingManual/KeysInfo: Collected keys appear in Keys and Treasures. Tap the KEYS panel to view them. Used keys remain in the collection when the game retains them.
PlayingManual/ReadingInfo: Open Files, tap a category and select a file. Tap the left or right side of the page to move through it. Tap the close icon to close the file.
PlayingManual/NavigateInfo: Open the map to view rooms and points of interest. Drag within the map to move the view. Map filters show or hide categories of icons.
PlayingManual/FiltersInfo: Tap the categories on the map's filter panel to show or hide helpful icons.
PlayingManual/GemsInfo: View gems in the Gems drawer. They can be sold to the Merchant for PTAS or combined with compatible treasures. Hold a gem, drag it onto a treasure with a matching socket and release.
PlayingManual/EarningPrizesInfo: Earn prizes by reaching high scores in Shooting Range minigames. Each game type has a limited set of prizes, and new Shooting Range rooms unlock more game types. Collect earned prizes from the counter with action.
PlayingManual/PrizesInfo: Earned Shooting Range prizes appear in the Prizes panel of Keys and Treasures. Tap the panel to view your collection.
PlayingManual/ChoosingGameInfo: At the Shooting Range, interact with the bell on the counter to start. Tap the displayed weapon type and game mode to choose a minigame.
PlayingManual/SellInfo: Choose SELL at the Merchant. Hold an item or treasure, drag it from the inventory onto the table and release. Tap SELL to confirm the sale.
PlayingManual/TuneUpInfo: Choose TUNE UP at the Merchant. Drag an upgradeable weapon onto the vise, then tap the available upgrades to choose the improvements.
PlayingManual/BuyInfo: Choose BUY at the Merchant and tap an item. Place the selected goods from the table into free inventory space, then tap BUY to confirm. Cases and treasure maps do not require space in the grid.
PlayingManual/WatchImageMainText: Hold the round health dial to raise your left hand.
PlayingManual/WatchInfo: The round dial shows your health. Hold it to raise your left hand and check health and ammunition on your wrist. Release to lower your hand. During gameplay, the ammo count appears only on your wrist.
Tutorials/WepManImShotgunInfo: Tap the <Red>long gun</> icon to select the shotgun. Aim and fire with the on-screen controls; the normal pump action prepares the next shot.
Tutorials/WepManImFirstAidInfo: Tap the <Red>medical bag</> icon at the top of the screen, then hold fire to use the First Aid Spray.
Tutorials/WepManSecond: Equipped weapons and items are available through the on-screen equipment icons.
Tutorials/WepManQsIntro: Select assigned weapons and items with their on-screen icons. The selected item remains equipped.
Tutorials/WepManQsWheelInfo: Use the on-screen equipment icons to choose an assigned item.
Tutorials/WepManQsPistolInfo: Tap the <Red>handgun</> icon to select the assigned handgun.
Tutorials/WepManQsToggleInfo: Tap the <Red>handgun</> icon to switch back to your handgun.
Tutorials/WepManQsKnifeInfo: Tap the <Red>knife</> icon to select the knife.
Tutorials/HelpInfoQuickSelect: <HelpDefault>Assign a handgun, long gun, grenade or healing item by holding it with your finger and dropping it onto its matching equipment slot. Assigned items become available through the on-screen equipment icons during gameplay.</>
Tutorials/HelpInfoFiles: <HelpDefault>Tap a category and file to read collected notes or manuals. Tap the left or right side to change pages. Tap the close icon to close the file.</>
Tutorials/HelpInfoMap: <HelpDefault>The map shows rooms and points of interest. Drag within the map to move the view. Open Filters to show or hide categories of icons.</>
Tutorials/HelpInfoFilters: <HelpDefault>Tap a category on the filter panel to show or hide its map icons.</>
Tutorials/HelpInfoGems: <HelpDefault>Gems can be sold or combined with compatible treasures. Hold a gem with your finger, drag it onto a treasure with a matching socket and release to combine them.</>
Tutorials/HelpInfoKeys: <HelpDefault>This panel shows collected keys and puzzle items. Tap the Keys and Treasures tabs to browse the collection.</>
Tutorials/HelpInfoTreasures: <HelpDefault>Treasures can be sold to the Merchant for PTAS. Compatible gems increase their value. Use the Keys, Treasures and Prizes tabs to view each collection.</>
Tutorials/HelpInfoBottleCaps: <HelpDefault>This panel shows prizes earned in Shooting Range challenges. Select the Prizes panel to browse your collection.</>
Tutorials/HelpInfoOverflow: <HelpDefault>Drag items onto this table to clear space while organizing the inventory. To discard an item permanently, tap Remove. The table must be empty before returning to gameplay or switching tabs.</>
Tutorials/AshFoundHeal: Protect Ashley and watch her health. Healing items can restore her condition.
Tutorials/AshFoundSelectFollow: Ashley can follow or wait. Keep her close when moving through dangerous areas.

Options/QuickComfortDesc:
Control preset
Choose a starting preset. Mobile gameplay uses continuous movement, swipe turning and first-person actions with either preset. Camera effects can be adjusted separately.
Options/MovementStyleDesc:
Movement
Mobile movement is continuous. Use the floating stick on the left to walk, strafe or move backwards. Older movement presets do not change the touch controls.
Options/MovementStickDesc:
Movement side
The floating movement stick is on the left. Swipe the right side of the screen to turn. This layout is fixed for touch controls.
Options/TurnStyleDesc:
Turning
Swipe the right side of the screen to turn continuously. Older turning presets do not change the touch camera.
Options/TurnAngleDesc:
Legacy turn step
This setting belongs to the older turning layout. The touch camera turns continuously by swiping, so this value does not set its turning angle.
Options/TurnSpeedDesc:
Legacy turn speed
This setting belongs to the older turning layout. Touch turning follows your swipe.
Options/Quick180TurnDesc:
Legacy quick turn
Automatic half-turns are disabled for touch controls. Swipe the right side of the screen to turn around.
Options/SteeringDesc:
Movement direction
Touch movement follows the camera direction. The older hand and fixed-direction presets do not change this mobile layout.
Options/HeadSteeringDesc:
Camera-relative movement
The mobile movement layout follows the camera direction.
Options/CombatStyleDesc:
Combat style
Mobile controls allow movement and strafing while aiming. The original restricted movement preset does not change the mobile layout.
Options/StrafingDesc:
Strafing
Side-to-side movement is available through the floating stick in the mobile layout.
Options/CameraFacingDesc:
Camera orientation
The mobile camera keeps your current view direction when returning to first person.
Options/BoatControlModeDesc:
Boat camera
The mobile boat layout uses the original third-person camera and the floating movement stick for steering. Older boat presets do not add a separate handle control.
Options/CinematicWindowDesc:
Full-screen cutscenes
Cutscenes fill the screen. Older window-size choices do not change this presentation.
Options/TunnelingDesc:
Tunneling
Darkens the edges of the view while moving or turning. Off by default on phones.
Options/CameraBobDesc:
Camera bob
Enable or disable camera movement while walking.
Options/CameraShakeDesc:
Camera shake
Enable or disable camera shake during heavy hits or explosions.
Options/ControllerRumbleDesc:
Vibration
Phone vibration for shots, hits and other game effects.
Options/ControllerRumbleMenusDesc:
Menu vibration
Short phone vibration when pointing at menu items.
Options/GrenadeStyleDesc:
Grenade handling
Select an assigned grenade, aim and tap fire to throw. Touch throwing uses automatic pin handling. The older manual choice does not add a separate pin control. This setting does not apply to eggs.
Options/ReloadStyleDesc:
Reload handling
Tap reload to perform the weapon's normal ammunition replacement and chambering. Touch reload handles ejection and insertion with either original reload preset.
Options/WeaponManagementDesc:
Equipment selection
Choose assigned weapons and items with their on-screen icons. Empty slots cannot be selected. The selected item stays equipped; no separate hold control is required.
Options/SelectionStickDesc:
Legacy selection side
This setting belongs to the original selection menu. Touch equipment selection uses the on-screen item icons.
Options/InspectObjectDesc:
Examine object
Automatic inspection shows information while an item is held in the inventory. The older manual setting requires an additional original input action; select Auto for touchscreen use.
Options/GameDifficultyDesc:
Game difficulty
Easy: enemies are easier to handle and ammunition is more abundant; some exploration areas are unavailable.

Normal: the original standard challenge.

Professional: stronger enemies and fewer ammunition drops.
Options/PlayingPositionDesc:
Camera height profile
Choose the original camera and equipment height layout. This setting changes the character anchor; it does not require you to change your physical playing position.
Options/PlayerHeightDesc:
Character height
Adjust the original camera height for the Adjusted height profile. This is a character layout value, not your physical height.
Options/YourHeightOffsetDesc:
Camera height offset
Adjust the original camera height offset for the Tracking baseline profile.
Options/UseHolsterOffsetsDesc:
Equipment layout offsets
Adjust the original chest and waist equipment attachment layout. Touch selection uses equipment icons; these offsets do not move the on-screen controls.
UIStrings/CustomizeDesc: <Default.Text>Set up the character's equipment and camera layout. Movement uses the floating stick; look around by swiping the right side of the screen.</>

UIStrings/CustomizeCurrentDesc:

UIStrings/CustomizeConfirmDesc: Setup is complete. Use the floating stick to move and swipe the right side of the screen to look around. Open Controls / Camera in Options to review the available settings.
UIStrings/CustomizePopupDesc: Apply the standard starting preset. Mobile controls use continuous movement and swipe turning. You can review camera settings later in Controls / Camera.
Tutorials/ChooseBoatChoice1Sub: This older preset is replaced by the mobile boat layout. Steering uses the floating movement stick.
Tutorials/ChooseBoatChoice2Sub: This older preset is replaced by the mobile boat layout. Steering uses the floating movement stick.

Tutorials/ChooseBoatEnd: The mobile boat layout uses the third-person camera and floating-stick steering.

PlayingManual/MercsCharactersKrauserInfo:
Jack Krauser is a military agent turned henchman for Albert Wesker. His powerful Blade Thrust special attack makes him a formidable asset on any mission.

<Red>Special Attack</>
His unique attack takes one minute to charge. When activated, his Plagas infection lets him dash forward and strike enemies in his path.
PlayingManual/MercsCharactersKrauserSpec:
SPECIAL ATTACK
Krauser has a unique Blade Thrust attack that takes one minute to charge. When activated, his Plagas infection lets him dash forward and strike enemies in his path.
Options/DominantHandDesc:
Dominant hand
Choose the character's main hand for equipped weapons and items.
